name: East Sussex
description: East Sussex is a county on the south coast of England known for its chalk landscapes, historic towns and coastline. Brighton and Hove is its largest urban centre, while the South Downs, Seven Sisters and towns such as Lewes and Hastings define much of its character.

places.name: Wealden
places.description: A large rural district in East Sussex covering the Ashdown Forest, inspiration for A.A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh, and the historic town of Battle, site of the 1066 Norman Conquest.

places.name: Brighton and Hove
places.description: A vibrant seaside city on the East Sussex coast, known for its Regency architecture, the exotic Royal Pavilion, and one of Britain's most famous LGBTQ+ communities.

places.name: Eastbourne
places.description: A genteel Victorian seaside resort on the East Sussex coast, known for its long promenade, pier, and proximity to the chalk cliffs of Beachy Head, one of England's most dramatic coastal viewpoints.

places.name: Hastings
places.description: A historic town on the East Sussex coast, forever linked to the 1066 Battle of Hastings fought just inland, with a fishing quarter of distinctive tall wooden net huts.

places.name: Lewes
places.description: A historic county town in East Sussex famous for its dramatic Bonfire Night celebrations, a Norman castle, and a compact, hilly high street of independent shops.

places.name: Rother
places.description: A rural district in East Sussex covering the historic town of Rye, with its cobbled medieval streets, and stretches of coastline and countryside near Bexhill and Battle. Rich in Cinque Ports and Norman Conquest history.
